question.prompt: For every triple \((a,b,c)\) of nonzero real numbers, form the number \[ \frac a{|a|}+\frac b{|b|}+\frac c{|c|}+\frac{abc}{|abc|}. \] The set of all numbers formed is

solutions.explanation:
For any nonzero real number \(u\), the quotient \(u/|u|\) is \(1\) when \(u>0\) and \(-1\) when \(u<0\). Thus only the signs of \(a,b,c\) matter. Their product is positive when an even number are negative and negative when an odd number are negative.

The expression is unchanged by reordering \(a,b,c\), so we can group every triple by its number of negative entries:

- No negative entries give \(1+1+1+1=4\).
- One negative entry gives \(-1+1+1-1=0\).
- Two negative entries give \(-1-1+1+1=0\).
- Three negative entries give \(-1-1-1-1=-4\).

Every allowed triple belongs to exactly one of these four cases. The values \(4,0,-4\) are attained by \((1,1,1)\), \((-1,1,1)\), and \((-1,-1,-1)\), respectively. Therefore the set of values is \(\{-4,0,4\}\), choice B.
solutions.title: Classify by the number of negative inputs
